module priority_encoder #(
    parameter WIDTH = 4,
    parameter LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0
)(
    input  wire [WIDTH-1:0] input_unencoded,
    output wire output_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(WIDTH)-1:0] output_encoded,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0] output_unencoded
);

parameter LEVELS = WIDTH > 2 ? $clog2(WIDTH) : 1;
parameter W = 2**LEVELS;

generate
    if (WIDTH == 256 && LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY == 0) begin : fast_256
        wire [15:0] group_valid;
        wire [15:0] no_higher_group;
        wire [15:0] group_selected;
        wire [15:0] local_selected [0:15];
        wire [15:0] low_terms [0:3];

        genvar g, b, k;
        for (g = 0; g < 16; g = g + 1) begin : groups
            assign group_valid[g] = |input_unencoded[g*16 +: 16];
            if (g == 15) begin : highest_group
                assign no_higher_group[g] = 1'b1;
            end else begin : other_group
                assign no_higher_group[g] = ~|group_valid[15:g+1];
            end
            assign group_selected[g] = group_valid[g] & no_higher_group[g];

            for (b = 0; b < 16; b = b + 1) begin : bits_in_group
                if (b == 15) begin : highest_bit
                    assign local_selected[g][b] = input_unencoded[g*16+b];
                end else begin : other_bit
                    assign local_selected[g][b] = input_unencoded[g*16+b]
                        & ~|input_unencoded[g*16+15:g*16+b+1];
                end

                if (g == 0 && b == 0) begin : zero_index
                    // The original decoder selects index zero even on empty input.
                    assign output_unencoded[0] = no_higher_group[0]
                        & ~|input_unencoded[15:1];
                end else begin : nonzero_index
                    assign output_unencoded[g*16+b] = no_higher_group[g]
                        & local_selected[g][b];
                end
            end

            for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin : local_encoding
                // Empty groups contribute zero without a group-valid gate.
                if (k == 0) begin : bit0
                    assign low_terms[k][g] = no_higher_group[g]
                        & (|(local_selected[g] & 16'haaaa));
                end else if (k == 1) begin : bit1
                    assign low_terms[k][g] = no_higher_group[g]
                        & (|(local_selected[g] & 16'hcccc));
                end else if (k == 2) begin : bit2
                    assign low_terms[k][g] = no_higher_group[g]
                        & (|(local_selected[g] & 16'hf0f0));
                end else begin : bit3
                    assign low_terms[k][g] = no_higher_group[g]
                        & (|(local_selected[g] & 16'hff00));
                end
            end
        end

        for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin : low_encoding
            assign output_encoded[k] = |low_terms[k];
        end
        assign output_encoded[4] = |(group_selected & 16'haaaa);
        assign output_encoded[5] = |(group_selected & 16'hcccc);
        assign output_encoded[6] = |(group_selected & 16'hf0f0);
        assign output_encoded[7] = |(group_selected & 16'hff00);
        assign output_valid = |group_valid;
    end else begin : original_parameter_fallback
        wire [W-1:0] input_padded = {{W-WIDTH{1'b0}}, input_unencoded};
        wire [W/2-1:0] stage_valid [LEVELS-1:0];
        wire [W/2-1:0] stage_enc [LEVELS-1:0];
        genvar l, n;
        for (n = 0; n < W/2; n = n + 1) begin : loop_in
            assign stage_valid[0][n] = |input_padded[n*2+1:n*2];
            if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb
                assign stage_enc[0][n] = !input_padded[n*2];
            end else begin : msb
                assign stage_enc[0][n] = input_padded[n*2+1];
            end
        end
        for (l = 1; l < LEVELS; l = l + 1) begin : loop_levels
            for (n = 0; n < W/(2*2**l); n = n + 1) begin : loop_compress
                assign stage_valid[l][n] = |stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1:n*2];
                if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb
                    assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                        stage_valid[l-1][n*2] ?
                        {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]} :
                        {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]};
                end else begin : msb
                    assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                        stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1] ?
                        {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]} :
                        {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]};
                end
            end
        end
        assign output_valid = stage_valid[LEVELS-1];
        assign output_encoded = stage_enc[LEVELS-1];
        assign output_unencoded = 1 << output_encoded;
    end
endgenerate

endmodule

`resetall
",
  "bottleneck": "The available evidence is the three supplied mapped STA paths, all ending at one-hot outputs at 2.60 ns. They share an initial reduction/control chain and a buffer, followed by a 0.58 ns mux2i and a 0.47 ns o2111a before final decode gates. Those two cells alone account for approximately 40% of total arrival time. Together with the original encode-then-shift RTL, this suggests that priority-selection control followed by one-hot decoding, including its loading, is a useful optimization target. The reports do not establish an exact RTL-to-cell correspondence or a serial arithmetic bottleneck.",
  "rewrite": "Specialize the evaluated instance into sixteen 16-bit groups. Compute local highest-set-bit selections and group occupancy in parallel. Each one-hot output is formed directly from its local selection and absence of higher occupied groups, eliminating its functional dependence on the encoded bus. Form the upper encoded nibble from the selected group and the lower nibble by reducing gated local encodings. Local encoded contributions are gated by absence of higher groups rather than by a separate group-valid condition, since empty local encodings already equal zero. Retain the original implementation as an elaboration-time fallback for other parameter configurations.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Hypothesis, not a measurement: direct one-hot generation should remove the late encode-to-decode dependency responsible for the reported endpoints. A roughly 10–25% reduction from 2.60 ns is a reasonable experimental target, but neither that range nor improvement is established. The encoded outputs or shared group-suppression nets could become the new maximum-arrival paths. Run the exact supplied synthesis, mapping and STA flow to determine the actual maximum data arrival.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The candidate exchanges the binary mux-tree and final decoder for local priority masks, group-suppression logic and OR-based encoding. Shared group reductions and small local masks offer a plausible route to staying below 8862.124480 um^2, but mapped area has not been measured. Overlapping reductions, buffering and group-control fanout can increase area or cause electrical violations. This is an unvalidated candidate: acceptance requires full equivalence, mapped area at or below the cap, and zero max-slew and max-capacitance violations under the specified flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module name, ports, widths, original parameter names and defaults are retained. The optimized branch applies to WIDTH=256 and LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY=0. For every nonzero binary input, exactly the highest set index is selected, output_valid is one, and output_encoded is that index. For all-zero input, group and local selections are zero, so output_valid=0 and output_encoded=0; the explicit index-zero equation makes output_unencoded exactly 256'b1. No invalid output is masked or treated as a don't-care. The design is entirely combinational, with no clocks, state, assumptions or input restrictions. These statements describe the intended Boolean equivalence; no formal proof or EDA validation has been run here."
}
